scope: Proposition 5.1 (Exact correction) of the manuscript “Smooth isometric immersions of closed surfaces into Euclidean four-space” (preprints/Smooth-isometric-immersions-of-closed-surfaces-into-Euclidean-four-space-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 333 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 1f0bf283be86c80b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 15. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let M be a closed smooth surface, and let h∗ be a smooth Riemannian metric on M. Fix background norms. There are positive integers R, N with the following property. Suppose that fz : M → R4 are smooth immersions for sufficiently small z > 0, and that ∥fz∥Cm = O(z−m ) (0 ≤ m ≤ R + 2), (5.1) ∥γ(fz) − h∗∥CR = O(zN ), (5.2) min p∈M max |u|=1 |Bfz (u, u)| ≥ c > 0. (5.3) Then, for all sufficiently small z, there is a smooth immersion e fz : M → R4 such that γ( e fz) = h∗, ∥ e fz − fz∥C2 = o(1). The integers R, N do not depend on the constants in (5.1)–(5.3). The threshold on z may depend on them. No regularity of the family with respect to z is required or asserted.
